records.name: Ion migration in metal-halide perovskites
records.summary: Mobile ionic defects can redistribute under electrical, thermal or illumination stress and are tightly connected to hysteresis, interfacial changes and long-term stability.

sources.title: Ion migration in perovskite solar cells
sources.note: 2026 review of ion-migration mechanisms, consequences and mitigation strategies.

data.principle: Metal-halide perovskites contain mobile ionic defects. Their redistribution can modify internal fields and interfaces, so time-dependent or bias-dependent device behavior may have an ionic contribution in addition to electronic transport.
data.implications: When hysteresis, drift during repeated JV scans, bias-history dependence or accelerated degradation is observed, ion migration is a plausible mechanism to test rather than an automatic conclusion. Compare scan direction/rate, stabilization behavior, temperature/light stress and interface changes.
data.cautions: Do not infer ion migration from a single anomalous JV curve. Separate ionic hypotheses from contact effects, measurement artifacts, shunts and ordinary electronic recombination.

records.name: ISOS stability assessment for perovskite photovoltaics
records.summary: Consensus ISOS-style protocols make stability measurements more comparable by recording stress conditions, device state and reporting details explicitly.

sources.title: Consensus statement for stability assessment and reporting for perovskite photovoltaics based on ISOS procedures
sources.note: Consensus stability-testing and reporting framework for perovskite photovoltaics.

data.principle: Stability claims are interpretable only when illumination, temperature, atmosphere, electrical load, encapsulation, preconditioning and measurement cadence are documented. ISOS procedures provide shared test families rather than a single universal lifetime test.
data.implications: For degradation or aging experiments, capture the stress protocol and metadata alongside performance over time. Prefer normalized retention plus absolute starting/final metrics and document interruptions or measurement-condition changes.
data.cautions: Do not compare lifetime numbers from unlike stress conditions as if they were equivalent. A protocol label without the actual conditions is insufficient provenance.

records.name: Surface passivation and non-radiative recombination
records.summary: Surface/interface passivation can reduce defect-assisted non-radiative recombination and improve optoelectronic quality, but treatment effects are interface- and process-dependent.

sources.title: Surface passivation of perovskite film for efficient solar cells
sources.note: Demonstrates PEAI surface passivation and reduction of non-radiative recombination in perovskite solar cells.

data.principle: Defect-rich surfaces and interfaces can provide non-radiative recombination pathways. Chemical or structural passivation may suppress these losses and can increase photoluminescence, quasi-Fermi-level splitting and device voltage when the interface remains electrically selective.
data.implications: When a passivation treatment improves Voc or PL-related indicators without a proportional current gain, reduced non-radiative loss is a useful hypothesis. Compare untreated controls, interface-sensitive measurements and reproducibility across devices.
data.cautions: A passivation layer can also change energetics, transport, morphology or contact resistance. Do not attribute every performance change solely to defect passivation.

records.name: Defect tolerance is conditional, not defect immunity
records.summary: Halide perovskites can tolerate some defects unusually well, while other defects, surfaces and interfaces still create harmful traps or ionic pathways.

sources.title: Multifaceted nature of defect tolerance in halide perovskites and emerging semiconductors
sources.note: 2025 review explaining several mechanisms and limits of defect tolerance.

data.principle: Defect tolerance does not mean that defects are irrelevant. The electronic depth, charge state, structural relaxation, concentration and location of a defect determine whether it is benign or strongly recombination-active.
data.implications: Interpret defect-related changes using multiple observables: PL/TRPL, voltage deficit, ideality/recombination signatures, morphology and interface information are more informative together than a single proxy.
data.cautions: Avoid the generic explanation “more defects” unless a measurement actually supports it. Bulk, grain-boundary and interface defects can have different effects.

records.name: Point defects couple electronic and ionic behavior
records.summary: Vacancies, interstitials and antisites can influence carrier recombination, doping, ionic transport and degradation depending on composition and operating conditions.

sources.title: Point defects in metal halide perovskites
sources.note: 2025 review of point-defect physics, characterization and implications in metal-halide perovskites.

data.principle: Native and extrinsic point defects can alter carrier density and recombination and can act as participants in ionic transport. Their populations and charge states depend on chemistry and processing, so the same nominal material can behave differently after changes in stoichiometry or thermal history.
data.implications: Composition/process comparisons should keep stoichiometry, precursor history and annealing metadata traceable. If electrical drift accompanies chemistry changes, test both electronic-defect and ionic explanations.
data.cautions: Assigning a specific microscopic defect requires dedicated evidence; ordinary JV/PL measurements alone rarely identify one unique vacancy, interstitial or antisite.

records.name: J–V hysteresis and stabilized power in perovskite solar cells
records.summary: A forward/reverse J–V mismatch can be a measurement-history effect in perovskite devices. Treat scan direction/rate as measurement context and prefer quasi-steady-state or MPP-tracked performance when judging device output.

sources.title: Consensus statement for stability assessment and reporting for perovskite photovoltaics based on ISOS procedures
sources.note: Consensus guidance discusses J–V hysteresis, quasi-steady-state measurements and MPP tracking for perovskite devices.

data.content: Do not interpret a single scan-direction PCE as an intrinsic material property when forward/reverse scans disagree. Compare scan direction and rate, look for stabilized or MPP-tracked output when available, and report the measurement protocol together with the metric.
data.cautions: Hysteresis alone does not identify one degradation mechanism and does not by itself prove that a device is unstable.

records.name: PLQY and quasi-Fermi-level splitting as recombination indicators
records.summary: Absolute photoluminescence quantum yield and quasi-Fermi-level splitting can diagnose non-radiative recombination losses in perovskite absorbers and interfaces when the measurement conditions are controlled.

sources.title: Hybrid perovskite films approaching the radiative limit with over 90% photoluminescence quantum efficiency
sources.note: Demonstrates the relationship between high PLQY, QFLS and reduced non-radiative losses in treated perovskite films.

sources.title: Visualization and suppression of interfacial recombination for high-efficiency large-area pin perovskite solar cells
sources.note: Uses absolute photoluminescence and QFLS analysis to distinguish bulk and interfacial recombination losses.

data.content: Higher PLQY or QFLS under comparable excitation and optical conditions is generally consistent with lower non-radiative recombination. Changes after adding a transport layer can reveal interface-related losses, but comparisons require matched excitation, sample geometry and analysis conditions.
data.cautions: PL intensity alone is not a universal proxy for device efficiency. Do not compare unmatched excitation conditions or infer a specific defect species from PLQY alone.

records.name: Champion device versus reproducible device distribution
records.summary: A best device is useful but insufficient for comparing experimental groups. Interpret champion performance together with replicate count, distribution, exclusions and measurement consistency.

sources.title: A checklist for photovoltaic research
sources.note: Calls for statistical evidence, average performance alongside best devices and careful reporting of characterization procedures.

sources.title: Consensus statement for stability assessment and reporting for perovskite photovoltaics based on ISOS procedures
sources.note: Recommends reporting sample counts and statistics because sample-to-sample and batch-to-batch variation matter.

data.content: When comparing REF and treatment groups, prioritize the full validated distribution and replicate coverage before making claims from the champion device. Keep excluded or anomalous measurements visible in provenance and distinguish exploratory patterns from reproducible effects.
data.cautions: A higher champion PCE does not by itself establish a better process, mechanism or reproducible population shift.
